# Charaf Eddine Benarab

### AI Researcher · Solutions Architect · Consultant

Artificial Intelligence Consultant and Solutions Architect specializing in low-level Deep Neural Network (DNN) architecture design, gradient optimization, and high-level AI product engineering — retrieval-augmented generation, multi-agent execution graphs, and context management systems for constrained inference environments. Based in Algiers, sometimes Kuala Lumpur.

My work spans two registers that are usually kept apart: **industry engagements** — architecting production RAG systems, agentic execution graphs, and on-premise LLM deployments under real compliance and hardware constraints — and **research and academic work** — Transformer architecture design, cross-modal representation learning, and neuro-symbolic approaches to context and memory, several of which have resulted in peer-reviewed publications. Each register disciplines the other: production constraints keep the research grounded, and the research keeps the production work from calcifying around whatever the current tooling happens to make easy.

## Current focus

Independent AI consultant, engaged as Chief AI Officer and Lead AI Architect. Most recently at **InfinitGraph**, where I directed the R&D pipeline for an agentic discovery platform and brought a 14B-parameter open-source model to production-grade benchmark targets typically assumed to require substantially larger models — achieved by displacing capability from the model onto a deterministic software layer around it, rather than by scaling the model itself.

## Technical program

**Context engineering as an alternative to scale.** The prevailing assumption in the field is that capability is a direct function of parameter count and compute. My work proceeds from the opposite premise: a language model is a probabilistic kernel embedded in a deterministic protocol, and a substantial share of what looks like "model capability" is properly a property of the surrounding system — token-budget enforcement, dynamic KV-cache management, prefix-caching, sliding-window attention, and structured context compression. Correctly engineered, this lets compact models operate at a fidelity typically reserved for far larger ones.

**Agentic execution graphs.** Stateful multi-agent systems designed as deterministic Directed Acyclic Graphs (LangGraph and comparable frameworks), with explicit conditional routing, node-level error handling, and parallel traversal. A system whose behavior cannot be audited node by node is not a system I consider production-ready.

**Hybrid retrieval architectures.** Retrieval-augmented generation combining dense vector search (Qdrant and comparable engines) with symbolic knowledge structures (Neo4j graph databases), on the premise that nearest-neighbor retrieval alone degrades once a corpus has real relational structure — citation graphs, patent families, regulatory hierarchies.

**Sovereign and air-gapped deployment.** A significant share of my engagements operate under infrastructure constraints that preclude hosted inference — regulatory, security, or hardware-driven. This constraint set is generative rather than limiting: it forces architectures that are local, auditable, and cheap to run, which tend to be better-engineered systems regardless of the constraint.
